newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan contractors urged to cut links with sokaiya.
newsitem.headline: Japan contractors urged to cut links with sokaiya.

text.p: Police on Wednesday urged Japanese construction companies to cut links with "sokaiya" corporate racketeers or gangsters, officials of a construction industry group told reporters.

A senior official in the criminal investigation bureau of the Metropolitan Police Department asked senior officials of the group, the Japan Federation of Construction Contractors, to stop subscribing to periodicals which are regarded as a key source of funds for the extortionists, the officials said.
"If you face any security problems by stopping (such subscriptions), the police are ready to deal with it," the police official was quoted as telling the meeting.

The request follows a high-profile racketeer pay-off scandal involving one of Japan's top commercial banks, the Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), and the nation's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Sokaiya extort money from firms by threatening to disclose management misdeeds or disrupt annual shareholders' meetings. Payoffs to sokaiya have been illegal since 1983.
The construction industry body, which has 64 member companies, reaffirmed its commitment to refrain from having any relations with sokaiya.
